messages:
Tom: Hey team — following up on the RFC about carving runtime into control-plane vs execution-plane services. I sketched a pragmatic migration we can try next quarter. Thoughts?
Priya: +1 to getting a small prototype. what are the minimal interfaces we need for phase 1?
Tom: Minimal: 1) job submission API (submitJob(jobSpec)), 2) KV cache control (claim/release prefixes), 3) health + tracing headers. gRPC v1.0 with proto versioning.
Carla: can you paste a quick proto sketch? helps unblock integration tests.
Tom: Sure — rough: ```proto
service RuntimeControl {
  rpc SubmitJob(SubmitRequest) returns (SubmitResponse);
  rpc GetJobStatus(JobId) returns (Status);
  rpc ClaimCache(ClaimRequest) returns (ClaimResponse);
}
```
Miguel: latency implications? adding RPCs between scheduler and worker might add 3-6ms per request if we do sync calls. need async paths for hot-path token gen.
Priya: agree — plan: control-plane calls for allocation and metadata only. execution-plane keeps token path local. control-plane only touches cold-start, eviction, scaling.
Jenna: product ask — no downtime for customer model pins. how do we guarantee consistent rollout while moving ownership?
Tom: migration approach: 1) run execution-plane in pass-through mode (current binary) behind a feature flag; 2) enable control-plane for new jobs only; 3) shadow traffic for existing jobs; 4) cutover when metrics stable.
Raj: infra notes — need cross-service tracing and a migration toggle in our deploy system. also will need a small metadata DB owned by control-plane (non-shared writes).
Carla: DB ownership is key. we should not allow both planes to write the same rows. propose: control-plane owns job metadata table; execution-plane has a read replica.
Miguel: batching semantics: execution-plane must expose a batch negotiation API so scheduler can pack similar requests. otherwise latency/cost will regress.
Priya: +1 batch-negotiation. add: versioned headers so old schedulers can talk to new execs during rollout.
Tom: decision checkpoint for RFC: implement control-plane with write ownership for job metadata + cache claims; execution-plane keeps token path and batch negotiation API. migration via feature-flagged pass-through then shadowing.
Jenna: timeline request — can we have an experimental prototype in 6 weeks?
Tom: sounds doable. action: Tom + Priya to own prototype, Carla to own integration tests, Raj to prep infra toggles.
Raj: I'll add a deploy toggle and a canary namespace. sre-bot will enforce rollout alarms.
sre-bot: AUTO: created canary/rt-split namespace and added basic uptime alerts (link: https://monitoring.internal/canary/rt-split).
Carla: I'll write a small test harness that simulates prefix cache pressure and verify claim/release correctness.
Miguel: once prototype exists we should run 24h perf runs on p3 and t4 to validate latency/regression.
Tom: cool — I'll open a PR with the proto + migration plan doc and tag you all. thanks! :thumbsup:
